museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium
title: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works from the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, with attention to how images organise belief, status and surprise.
introduction:
A gallery full of paintings is a reasonable place to begin a guide to the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium. In Teniers's picture, however, it is also a display of ownership: the small people stand among an extraordinary quantity of objects. Other works here disturb the habits through which recognisable things are assigned meaning. Magritte repaints a classical cast; Bruegel combines familiar body parts into unfamiliar creatures; an almost invisible fall unsettles a broad landscape.

These twenty works do not tell a simple story of realism giving way to fantasy. The portraits and judicial scenes are constructed presentations too. What changes is how openly each picture exposes the arrangement.
visitNote: The Royal Museums’ collections occupy several departments. The Fin-de-Siècle and Modern museums are currently inaccessible as separate museums; selected works are being integrated into the Old Masters route. Check current displays before visiting. This guide describes collection works, not a promise that all twenty are on view.

works.title: Archduke Leopold Wilhelm in His Gallery
works.catalogueTitle: Archduke Leopold Wilhelm of Austria in his Gallery
works.credit: David Teniers the Younger. Archduke Leopold Wilhelm of Austria in his Gallery. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/david-teniers-the-younger/archduke-leopold-wilhelm-of-austria-in-his-gallery-1651
works.description: Pictures cover the room so thoroughly that looking at one means passing over others. The archduke and his companions become relatively small within this accumulation. Teniers records a way of possessing and displaying art as much as individual paintings: the crowded arrangement makes a collector's abundance itself available to be admired.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: The Copper Handcuffs
works.catalogueTitle: Copper handcuffs
works.credit: René Magritte. Copper handcuffs. WikiArt source label: Rene Magritte Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/rene-magritte/copper-handcuffs-1931
works.license: Rene Magritte Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Colour divides the cast where its sculptural form would normally remain continuous. The familiar outline of the Venus de Milo survives, but the yellow torso and dark blue drapery establish a new set of boundaries. Magritte's intervention does not depend on concealing the source. Recognition is precisely what allows the imposed divisions to become conspicuous.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Dario de Regoyos Playing the Guitar
works.catalogueTitle: Dario de Regoyos Playing the Guitar
works.credit: Théo van Rysselberghe. Dario de Regoyos Playing the Guitar. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/theo-van-rysselberghe/dario-de-regoyos-playing-the-guitar-1882
works.description: The guitar crosses the sitter's body and gives his arms something to do. Its warmer colour also separates it from the dark clothes, so the activity shapes the portrait both physically and visually. Regoyos is presented through an instrument held in use, rather than through an accessory placed nearby solely to describe his interests.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Doge Alvise IV Mocenigo Appearing to the People in Saint Mark’s
works.catalogueTitle: Doge Alvise IV Mocenigo Appears to the People in St. Mark's Basilica
works.credit: Francesco Guardi. Doge Alvise IV Mocenigo Appears to the People in St. Mark's Basilica. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/francesco-guardi/doge-alvise-iv-mocenigo-appears-to-the-people-in-st-mark-s-basilica-1777
works.description: The ceremony is small in relation to the basilica that contains it. Arches and columns carry the view upward while patches of light keep the architectural mass from becoming immovable. Guardi makes public authority dependent on its setting: the gathering has significance, but the building supplies much of the scale through which that significance is seen.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Drunken Silenus with Two Bacchantes
works.catalogueTitle: Drunken Silenus, supported by two bacchantes
works.credit: Drunken Silenus, supported by two bacchantes. WikiArt; Anthony van Dyck. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Silenus's body has become a weight that other bodies must manage. The figures crowd together because supporting him leaves little room for separation. This physical problem gives the mythological scene its immediate intelligibility. Bent limbs and gathered drapery describe the effort more directly than an explanation of each participant's identity would.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Model in Backlight
works.catalogueTitle: Model in Backlight
works.credit: Pierre Bonnard. Model in Backlight. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pierre-bonnard/model-in-backligh-1908
works.description: The bright window does not turn the figure into the room's most clearly described object. Pattern, warm interior colour and cooler light compete around the body, making it part of a larger field of surfaces. The picture can be read by following those interruptions rather than treating the room as a passive setting for a nude.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Natural Encounters
works.catalogueTitle: Natural encounters
works.credit: René Magritte. Natural encounters. WikiArt source label: Rene Magritte Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/rene-magritte/natural-encounters-1945
works.license: Rene Magritte Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The encounter is plainly arranged even though its participants are impossible. Red robes give the birdlike beings something like bodily solidity; openings onto sky establish a space around them. The calm separation of forms matters. Strangeness remains available for sustained looking instead of being concealed in darkness or a confused rush of action.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Antoine, the Bastard of Burgundy
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of Antoine, bastard of Burgundy
works.credit: Portrait of Antoine, bastard of Burgundy. WikiArt; Rogier van der Weyden. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The arrow occupies the space in front of the sitter, and the gold chain follows his neckline. These objects give the otherwise restrained portrait a public register of status and allegiance. The dark clothes keep their signals distinct. The face remains controlled, offering no narrative that would explain how this formal presentation was received.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Madame Charles Maus
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of Madame Charles Maus
works.credit: Théo van Rysselberghe. Portrait of Madame Charles Maus. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/theo-van-rysselberghe/portrait-of-madame-charles-maus-1890
works.description: The dark dress retains a substantial outline while small touches of colour break up the lighter room. Van Rysselberghe allows two kinds of seeing to coexist: the recognition of a seated woman and awareness of the separate marks forming her surroundings. The transition between dress and interior is where their difference becomes easiest to follow.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Johannes Schöner
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of Magdeburg Theologian Dr. Johannes Schöner
works.credit: Lucas Cranach the Elder. Portrait of Magdeburg Theologian Dr. Johannes Schöner. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/lucas-cranach-the-elder/portrait-of-magdeburg-theologians-dr-johannes-sch%C3%B6ner-1529
works.description: Hair, fur and the red garment crowd close to the sitter's head, supplying several kinds of texture within a compact portrait. The hands remain together below. With little architectural setting to describe him, the figure's authority rests on this tightly organised presentation rather than on a surrounding office, landscape or collection of possessions.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Octave Maus
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of Octave Maus
works.credit: Théo van Rysselberghe. Portrait of Octave Maus. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/theo-van-rysselberghe/portrait-of-octave-maus-1885
works.description: The full-length format gives the sitter's bearing as much work to do as his facial likeness. His dark silhouette holds its shape against flowers and furnishings whose outlines are softer. Compare this with the later portrait of Madame Charles Maus: Van Rysselberghe changes the treatment of the room without abandoning the distinction between figure and setting.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: The Fall of the Rebel Angels
works.catalogueTitle: The Fall of the Rebel Angels
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Fall of the Rebel Angels. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pieter-bruegel-the-elder/the-fall-of-the-rebel-angels-1562
works.description: The upper figure can be recognised relatively quickly; the lower mass takes longer to separate into creatures. Familiar wings, shells and limbs join bodies that do not behave like familiar animals. That change in legibility gives the fall a pictorial form: order is progressively lost as attention enters the dense, hybrid crowd.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: The Temptation of Saint Anthony
works.catalogueTitle: The Temptation of St. Anthony
works.credit: Salvador Dalí. The Temptation of St. Anthony. WikiArt source label: Salvador Dali Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/salvador-dali/the-temptation-of-st-anthony
works.license: Salvador Dali Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The animals appear heavy enough to carry architecture, yet their extremely thin legs offer implausible support. The kneeling saint's raised cross confronts a procession whose scale is difficult to measure. Dalí keeps the objects clearly described while breaking the ordinary relations between weight, size and balance that would make them physically possible.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Yawning Man
works.catalogueTitle: Yawning Man (disputed attribution)
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. Yawning Man (disputed attribution). WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pieter-bruegel-the-elder/yawning-man-disputed-attribution-1563
works.description: A yawn temporarily reorganises the whole face: the mouth opens, the eyes close and the upper lip rises. It is an action poorly suited to a dignified formal likeness, which makes its isolation here especially pointed. The work's uncertain attribution should remain visible; the specificity of the expression does not resolve who painted it.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Three Studies of a Lady with a Hat
works.catalogueTitle: Three Studies of a Lady with a Hat
works.credit: Three Studies of a Lady with a Hat. WikiArt; Jean-Antoine Watteau. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The same hat-wearing figure appears at different angles, allowing the poses to be compared without pretending they occurred simultaneously in one room. Bare areas keep the studies apart. The sheet preserves alternatives, showing how clothing changes its shape when a body turns and how much a finished pose leaves outside its final arrangement.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Allegory of Abundance
works.catalogueTitle: Allegory of Abundance
works.credit: Jacob Jordaens. Allegory of Abundance. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/jacob-jordaens/allegory-of-abundance
works.description: Fruit, children and overlapping bodies fill the space so densely that abundance becomes a condition of the composition. The turning female figure is part of that accumulation, rather than a detached symbol above it. Repeated rounded shapes connect living bodies and produce, giving the allegorical subject an emphatically material form.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: The Cook
works.catalogueTitle: Cook in front of the Stove
works.credit: Pieter Aertsen. Cook in front of the Stove. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The cook meets the viewer's attention while meat, vegetables and vessels occupy a substantial foreground. These things describe the work around her, but her scale and outward gaze prevent the picture from becoming simply an arrangement of provisions. Kitchen labour is presented through a figure able to hold the image as firmly as its plentiful objects.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: The Depths of Pleasure
works.catalogueTitle: Depths of pleasure
works.credit: René Magritte. Depths of pleasure. WikiArt source label: Rene Magritte Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/rene-magritte/depths-of-pleasure-1948
works.license: Rene Magritte Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Loose outlines and rough areas of red, orange and blue differ from the smooth clarity associated with many of Magritte's other paintings. The female form remains recognisable without settling into a continuous surface. Seen beside *Natural Encounters*, this work prevents a single finish or manner from standing in for the artist's whole practice.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: The Justice of Emperor Otto: The Ordeal by Fire
works.catalogueTitle: Justice of the Emperor Otto: The Ordeal by Fire
works.credit: Dieric Bouts. Justice of the Emperor Otto: The Ordeal by Fire. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The tiled hall and upright witnesses give the ordeal an appearance of measured procedure. Yet the test concerns bodily danger, not merely a formal exchange of words. The tension lies between that regulated setting and the means by which a claim is judged. Bouts makes the audience's presence an essential part of the event.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

works.title: Landscape with the Fall of Icarus
works.catalogueTitle: Landscape with the Fall of Icarus
works.credit: Pieter Bruegel the Elder. Landscape with the Fall of Icarus. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The ploughman and ships make the landscape readily readable before the small legs in the water interrupt it. Knowing the title changes the hierarchy: an easily missed incident becomes the named subject. Attribution and dating remain unresolved. The museum announced new technical research in 2026, so the painting should not be presented as an unquestioned Bruegel original.
works.museum: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

closingSections.title: Separate a collection from a route
paragraphs: These works belong to a museum organisation with different collections and display arrangements. Check the relevant museum and individual work before visiting. In Artline, comparing dates can clarify how far apart these experiments were made; resemblance alone does not establish that one artist knew another's work.
